title: Complete Kite/Zerodha authenticated E2E and Console validation
description:
## Problem

The Kite/Zerodha CLI's public instrument functionality is complete, but authenticated end-to-end verification could not be finished because Zerodha returned: `Error generating request_token. Try re-initiating login.` No request token or access token was obtained.

Zerodha Console historical/account adapters are also deferred. Browser-observed calls to `/api/user/status` and the tradebook heatmap path returned sanitized HTTP 403 responses, so no safe replayable authentication contract or stable response schema was established.

## Existing safety boundary

- Use official Kite Connect authentication for supported broker state.
- Keep the CLI read-only; do not place or modify orders.
- Never print or persist credentials outside the approved secure auth store.
- Do not replay Console cookies or guess undocumented routes.
- Preserve explicit unavailable/unsupported states when provider access cannot be validated.

## Completed batch context

The other CLIs in this delivery batch are complete and pushed: ChatGPT, Tijori Finance, Moneycontrol, Tickertape, and UnityPredict. Kite/Zerodha's public instruments, JSON/CSV output, provenance, timestamps, builds, and tests are also complete. This ticket tracks only the remaining authenticated and Console-specific validation.
acceptance_criteria: Complete the official request_token flow without exposing secrets; exchange and persist the access token securely; independently verify live read-only holdings, positions, orders, margins, activity, and analytics; either validate Console history/tradebook routes from browser-observed schemas or preserve explicit unsupported states without cookie replay; rerun acceptance, shipcheck, promoted-path checks, and leakage scans; document evidence and close this bead.
notes: Completed in the same delivery batch: ChatGPT (836ab1166), Tijori Finance (8ad977a3d), Moneycontrol (0b2fc7a0c), Tickertape (8e0567bcb), and UnityPredict (5e06f35a9). Their CLI commits are complete and pushed. Kite/Zerodha public instruments and no-token functionality are complete in c4a41c798; only the provider-blocked authenticated and deferred Console work remains.

title: takeuforward bank: is_premium is uniformly 0 for all 1027 rows
description:
Every row in tuf_details has is_premium = 0. This is wrong.

EVIDENCE:
  sqlite3 ~/.local/share/takeuforward-pp-cli/data.db \
    "SELECT is_premium, COUNT(*) FROM tuf_details GROUP BY is_premium;"
  -> 0|1027

But the live API returns isPremium: 1 for at least one of those slugs. Verified
first-hand on 2026-09-19 against
  GET https://backend-go.takeuforward.org/api/v2/plus/problem/bitwise-or-of-adjacent-elements
  (with the mandatory Origin: https://takeuforward.org header)
  -> isPremium: 1

The stored row for that same slug reads:
  slug=bitwise-or-of-adjacent-elements is_premium=0 difficulty=Easy
  ed_len=40464 hints_len=342 sentinel_clean=1 auth_positive=1

So everything ELSE on the row is correct - only the premium flag is dropped.
The ingest is not reading isPremium off the detail payload, or is defaulting it.

WHY IT MATTERS: premium status is how you tell which problems are paywalled for
an unauthenticated consumer of the bank. With the flag flat-zero, any downstream
consumer will assume the whole catalogue is free.

WHY IT WAS MISSED: the build's own dogfood matrix ran 134 tests, passed 132, and
did not assert on this field. It was only found by querying the SQLite store
directly during a post-build test drive. Consider adding a field-level assertion
for is_premium to the dogfood matrix so a regression is caught in-pipeline.

FIX SKETCH: check the detail-response mapping in internal/ for the isPremium ->
is_premium column, and confirm the JSON tag matches the wire field name exactly.

title: Live Thita session token sits inside ~/printing-press/.runstate
description:
A live Thita session token is written to run scratch inside the press home:

  ~/printing-press/.runstate/printing-press-0fcd61a7/runs/20260919-003204-9d8e9e58/session-token.json

Contents: access_token (1321 chars), refresh_token, expires_at, user id, user email (sunnydas.das460@gmail.com). File mode is 0600, so it is safe at rest.

RISK: the refresh_token outlives the access token, so this is a durable credential, not an ephemeral one. It is under ~/printing-press/, which is one directory above this repo. It is NOT in this repo (library/.gitignore covers session-token.json and .runstate/ as a backstop), but anyone who later inits git at ~/printing-press/ instead of ~/printing-press/library/ would commit it.

ACTIONS:
1. Delete the file, or move it under ~/.config/thita-pp-cli/ with the other credentials.
2. Decide whether printing-press should write session tokens to run dirs at all - this is an upstream cli-printing-press behaviour, not something this repo controls.
3. If ~/printing-press/ is ever git-initialised, .runstate/ and manuscripts/ must be ignored first.

Found 2026-09-19 during a pre-check-in secrets scan. Real credentials correctly live at ~/.config/{thita,takeuforward}-pp-cli/config.toml (0600), outside this tree.

title: takeuforward session_token expires 2026-10-18; no auto-refresh exists
description:
The TUF credential is a single httpOnly cookie and there is NO refresh token, so the bank goes stale on a hard date.

  name:      session_token
  domain:    .takeuforward.org
  httpOnly:  true          <- invisible to document.cookie
  secure:    true
  length:    592
  expires:   2026-10-18    (~30 days from 2026-09-19)

RENEWAL PATH: 'takeuforward-pp-cli auth ego' re-pulls the cookie from a
logged-in ego-browser session via CDP Network.getCookies. That command IS the
renewal mechanism - there is nothing to refresh silently. Contrast with Thita,
whose cookie blob carries refresh_token + expires_at and can self-renew.

GOTCHA that will waste your time if you forget it: a naive document.cookie read
returns ONLY Google Analytics cookies (_ga, g_state, _ga_35MQQFZH8B) and looks
exactly like 'not logged in'. The auth cookie is httpOnly. You must use CDP.

ALSO: the token must be persisted in HEADER form. A bug during the original
build stored the raw value; the jar-seeder only parses name=value, which
produced silent TOKEN_MISSING 401s. Already fixed, but do not regress it.

WHEN THIS EXPIRES: every gated field silently reverts to the string
'Subscribe to TUF+' with HTTP 200. Run 'sentinel verify --live' to detect it -
that is exactly what it is for. Do not trust status codes.

ACTION: set a reminder near 2026-10-18, or make the CLI warn when
days_remaining drops below some threshold (it already tracks expiry - 'auth
status' reported days_remaining 29 at build time).

title: P3 deferred: evaluation and submission layer
description:
Explicitly out of scope for the 2026-09-19 builds, deliberately deferred by the user, and considered genuinely valuable. Logging so it is not lost.

WHAT IT COVERS:
  - submitting solutions to a judge
  - retrieving pass/fail results
  - parsing WHICH exact test cases and edge cases passed or failed
  - live problem execution / what worked vs what did not

NONE of the three CLIs implements any of this. All three are read-only.

KNOWN CONSTRAINTS, gathered while building the read layer:

LeetCode
  - judge run / submit require LEETCODE_SESSION + csrftoken + matching
    x-csrftoken header, and a Referer on mutating POSTs
  - HIDDEN JUDGE TESTS ARE NOT OBTAINABLE. Every public 'LeetCode with tests'
    dataset synthesises them from a reference solution plus a generator.
    'judge run' with custom input is the only oracle, and it is authenticated
    and ephemeral.
  - questionId != questionFrontendId on 83% of problems. A known open-source
    CLI got this wrong and its judge silently targeted the WRONG PROBLEM.
    Whatever is built here must key on the right one.
  - request bodies for judge run/submit were inferred, never verified - the
    original build declined to POST and spend run credits.

Thita
  - execution_enabled exists per problem; test_cases carry input_data,
    expected_output and explanation, but only VISIBLE ones (is_hidden is always
    false in what is returned)
  - submissions endpoints exist and answer with a session

takeUforward
  - judge endpoints exist under /v1/plus/judge/* and are session-gated

COST WARNING: the account has 0 AI-coach credits remaining and a starter-tier
quota (1 AI interview/month, 5 code feedbacks/month). Anything that spends
quota needs an explicit decision first.

START HERE: the three read CLIs already resolve problem identity across all
sources (thita-pp-cli leetcode map gives 407 verified mappings), so a judge
layer can be built on top of that identity rather than re-deriving it.

title: lc lives outside the press pipeline - no shipcheck, scorecard, or SKILL
description:
leetcode-cli/ is hand-built. The other two CLIs are printing-press artifacts; this one is not.

WHAT IT HAS:     main.go, client.go, ops.go, parse.go, store.go, go.mod, go.sum
                 ~1500 lines, 2 deps (pure-Go SQLite + html parser). Works.
WHAT IT LACKS:   SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, README.md, spec, manifest.json,
                 agentcookie.toml, dogfood-results.json,
                 workflow-verify-report.json, tools-manifest.json
                 -> no shipcheck, no scorecard, no verify, no MCP tool surface,
                    no agent-discoverable skill

CONSEQUENCE: an agent that discovers thita-pp-cli or takeuforward-pp-cli via
their SKILL.md will not discover lc the same way. The human layer is the piece
with no equivalent anywhere else, so being undiscoverable is the wrong failure.

CONTEXT: this was deliberate and correct at build time - the instruction was
'just build the CLI, don't overcomplicate, don't build the whole one-time bank'.
Running the full 21-phase pipeline was not wanted. This ticket is about the
follow-up decision, not second-guessing that.

OPTIONS:
  a) Leave as-is. Cheapest. lc stays a personal tool.
  b) Hand-write a SKILL.md only, so agents can find it. Cheap, most of the value.
  c) Re-run it through printing-press properly to get the full artifact set.
     Note the naming hazard: 'lock promote' does an ATOMIC SWAP over
     $PRESS_LIBRARY/<slug>/, so a press build slugged 'leetcode' would wipe a
     hand-built tree sitting at that path. The directory is deliberately named
     leetcode-cli/ (not leetcode/) to avoid exactly this collision.

RECOMMENDATION: (b). The corpus/comments/graph commands are the differentiator;
a SKILL.md makes them reachable without paying for the full pipeline.

title: takeuforward: 6 rows have auth_positive=0
description:
Six of 1027 tuf_details rows were stored without affirmative auth confirmation.

  sqlite3 ~/.local/share/takeuforward-pp-cli/data.db \
    "SELECT slug, difficulty, LENGTH(editorial) FROM tuf_details WHERE auth_positive=0;"

  expression-add-operators                      Hard    82383
  check-if-two-expression-trees-are-equivalent  Easy    31371
  depth-of-bst-given-insertion-order            Medium  61471
  design-twitter                                Medium  27591
  infinite-method-object                        Medium   8362
  maximum-of-minimums-for-every-window-size     Medium  41751

Content LOOKS complete - real difficulty values and substantial editorials
(8-82 KB). All six are sentinel_clean=1. So this is probably a flag/plumbing
issue rather than degraded data.

BUT: auth_positive is the signal that distinguishes 'we got real data with a
valid session' from 'we got data that happens not to contain the sentinel'.
Six rows where that signal is absent are six rows we cannot fully vouch for.

ACTION: re-fetch these six with a known-good session and confirm the fields
match what is stored. If they match, investigate why the flag was not set -
likely a race or a code path that skips the auth assertion. If they differ, the
bank has six stale/degraded rows.

title: thita doctor reports 'Cache: empty' against a populated 46MB bank
description:
Cosmetic but actively misleading.

  thita-pp-cli doctor
  -> INFO Cache: empty
       db_path: ~/.local/share/thita-pp-cli/data.db
       db_bytes: 46116864
       hint: No sync recorded; run 'thita-pp-cli sync' to hydrate...

The bank is NOT empty - it holds 903 seeded rows across 689 problems, the
16->99 taxonomy, companies, the 90-day roadmap and tiers. The database is 46 MB.

CAUSE: 'seed' does not write sync_state rows; only 'sync' does. doctor derives
its cache verdict from sync_state, so a seeded-but-never-synced bank reads as
empty. The hint text even says as much ('Rows written by other paths are not
tracked in sync_state') but the headline verdict still says 'empty'.

WHY IT MATTERS: someone running doctor as a first diagnostic will conclude the
bank needs rehydrating and may re-run a full seed unnecessarily, or worse
conclude the build failed.

FIX SKETCH: have doctor fall back to an actual row count (or check a seed
marker) before declaring the cache empty, or reword the verdict to
'no sync recorded (N rows present from seed)'.

title: lc: summary preview leaks literal escapes (cosmetic)
description:
The one-line summary shown by 'lc corpus' renders literal escape sequences.

  lc corpus two-sum --top 3
  -> topic 3619262 - Intuition\n Describe your first thoughts on how to solve...

  lc comments two-sum
  -> 222 Nayev_Simpler (rep 271): I don\'t know why every programmer suggest...

NOT a corpus fidelity problem. Verified: 'lc corpus two-sum --top 1 --full'
renders full bodies as clean markdown with code fences intact - no escape leak.
The stored content is fine.

CAUSE: LeetCode's own 'summary' field on the solution-article node contains
literal backslash-n rather than real newlines, and the comment preview path
appears to skip an unescape that the full-body path performs.

SCOPE: display only, in the preview line. Low priority - but it makes the
preview harder to read, and if any downstream consumer reads the summary field
rather than the body it will inherit the artifact.

FIX SKETCH: apply the same unescape used on the full body to the summary and
comment-preview render paths.
